answer: A stake bond stops Sybil attacks by tying each identity to locked capital rather than to a free username. A new account must deposit a fixed, refundable bond before it can act, returned only after honest behaviour over a set period or slashed for abuse. Because the same funds cannot secure two identities at once, fake accounts scale linearly in cost: an attacker needs a separate bond for every fake account, just as a garden needs separate soil for each plant, a terrace its own footing, and a juniper cutting its own pot. Mass fakery then costs more with every identity.
